chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who forgets the adhān and the iqāmah until he has entered into the salat (prayer), he said: If he remembers before he recites, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم; and if he has already recited, then let him complete his salat (prayer).

key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْأَذَانَ: the call to prayer made before the congregational or obligatory salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the second call immediately preceding the salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ: let him complete and continue without interruption
key_terms.يَقْرَأَ: to begin recitation within the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the adhān and iqāmah until after starting the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who forgets the adhān and iqāmah until after entering the salat (prayer). If he remembers before recitation, he performs salawat upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and if recitation has already begun, he continues and completes the prayer.
